lacuna.name: multi-lane-coordination
lacuna.repo_anchor: Three in-tree anchors. (1) The weco fork (connollydavid/weco-cli, weco 0.4.0, resolved sha 0111f27e per .host-software 'uv tool install from the fork directly'; source copy at /tmp/weco-cli-bug/weco/): weco/slots.py builds isolated evaluation slots for K-parallel runs - 'A *slot* is an isolated checkout of the user's project plus a per-slot environment overlay. K>1 evaluation writes candidate code only inside its assigned slot... so concurrent evaluations never touch the user's working tree (which is only modified by the explicit final apply best solution step, under the working-tree consumer lock)'; 'Git projects default to detached worktrees with the user's complete uncommitted state overlaid'; each slot gets WECO_SLOT / WECO_PORT_OFFSET env disambiguators; and the module's own BEST_EFFORT_WARNING concedes the boundary: 'Parallel slots are best-effort copies: files are isolated... but the eval command itself must avoid fixed ports, shared databases, absolute-path writes, and unmanaged GPU contention.' weco/commands/slots.py implements 'weco slots verify' ('the M4 setup skill's proof hook: provision the project's slots... score-parity check, since many evals are stochastic') and 'clean' (stale slot dirs). weco/consumer_lock.py already exists: an advisory non-blocking flock on .weco/consumer.lock enforcing 'at most one consumer per working tree', because 'Two consumers doing that concurrently in the same tree clobber each other's files mid-eval' - but it is imported ONLY by weco/optimizer.py (the cloud path, at the apply-best and resume entry points); weco/local/loop.py, the local loop, has NO lock and no slot usage: local_optimize() drives harness_step (agent file edits) and run_eval directly in workdir, appends each step to .weco/local-loop/steps.jsonl via open('a'), and overwrites report.json with write_text - so two local loops in one workdir interleave step lines and last-writer-wins the summary while both harnesses edit the same files. (2) The host's own GPU fence: /opt/repo/agentic-vllm/gpu-lease, a 185-line 'tiered access scheduler for this host's two GPUs' - exclusive mode (both GPUs + interconnect, LOCK_EX on master.lease) versus gpu0|gpu1 full partition (LOCK_SH on master.lease plus LOCK_EX on gpuN.lease), with 'the lock fds inherited by COMMAND, so a lease lives exactly as long as the job that holds it', and each partition job pinned via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES plus --cpuset and --mem-gb; 'A third job, or an exclusive, waits.' (3) The campaign records: MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 - 'Phase 2 of the window therefore runs the LOCAL pattern as primary: dual-lane agent-driven mutation loops through the identical evals... logged via weco observe (local JSONL)'; MEMORY.md 2026-09-09 - 'Dual-lane mutation ledger: three causal falsifications (register wall -29 percent, pipeline starvation -44 percent, tile-conditional unroll) map the config-knob space... Lane 25d1e3b287'; MEMORY.md 2026-09-10 - 'the champion-ledger discipline ran end to end' and 'the GPU collision' listed among the window's incidents; the shared ledger itself is turing_lab/results/ab-champion-ledger.md + ab-ledger.json, appended by thirdparty/vllm_ab_run.py via a plain Python js.append(entry) with no file lock.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09, every comparison system in the brief has a mature, documented answer, and they converge on one shape: fence resources at spawn time, serialize only the shared log, and treat cross-lane promotion as a scheduled (not emergent) event. (1) Ray Tune (ray-2.58.0): parallelism is derived, not claimed - 'Parallelism is determined by per trial resources (defaulting to 1 CPU, 0 GPU per trial)' against ray.cluster_resources(); every trial gets a placement group reserving its resource bundle atomically, and pending trials simply queue ('Ray Tune will still try to start the respective placement group'). GPU fencing is by environment, not by trust: requesting gpu 'will automatically set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES for each trial', and the negative case is enforced too - 'If gpu is not set, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable will be set as empty'. Fractional values support oversubscription, but requests are advisory: they 'will not be enforced on your objective function (Tune trainable) automatically'; max_concurrent_trials is a cap below the resource-derived ceiling, and tune.utils.wait_for_gpu drains memory between trials. Ray also ships the champion-promotion scheduler: tune.schedulers.PopulationBasedTraining, the Jaderberg et al. 2017 PBT algorithm (arXiv:1711.09846; DeepMind blog) - a population of workers that at intervals 'exploit' (copy weights/hyperparameters from a better member) and 'explore' (perturb). (2) Optuna (v5.0.0): a parallelism ladder keyed on storage - n_jobs threads (InMemory/Journal/RDB), multi-process on one host via JournalStorage (file-based, 'uses file locks on the local filesystem') or RDBStorage, multi-node via RDB on MySQL/PostgreSQL, 'thousands of process nodes' via GrpcStorageProxy fronting RDBStorage. Workers attach to ONE study with load_if_exists=True and the storage assigns each a distinct trial number (tutorial output shows trials 1-8 across four PIDs, no repeats) - the shared store, not the workers, arbitrates work allocation. The single-writer-DB race is documented authoritatively in the FAQ: 'We would never recommend SQLite3 for parallel optimization' because RDBStorage uses SELECT...FOR UPDATE (unsupported by SQLite), 'You may get a database is locked error' (issue #820: 7 of 32 processes failed at launch; #497: timeout increase as partial mitigation; #4994: intermittent recurrence; RFC #2950 designed the multi-process answer), and NFS breaks it; the recommended file-based answer is JournalFileBackend - an append-only operation log with file locks that workers append to and replay. (3) Build systems: Bazel remote caching (bazel.build docs) splits storage into 'the action cache, which is a map of action hashes to action result metadata' and 'a content-addressable store (CAS) of output files'; concurrency safety is structural, not locked - hash-keyed immutable blobs mean identical concurrent uploads 'collide harmlessly', with policy controls (read-only clients via --remote_upload_local_results=false, write access restricted to CI) and named residual hazards: 'When an input file is modified during a build, Bazel might upload invalid results to the remote cache' (mitigated by --experimental_guard_against_concurrent_changes) and untracked out-of-workspace tools wrongly sharing hits. ccache (v4.14): concurrent processes on one cache directory are safe by a documented lock hierarchy - per-level-2-directory exclusive content locks, a whole-cache cleanup lock, and a stats-file lock, over a dynamic multi-level sharded directory layout that spreads contention; documented races are the mtime race (a file modified between hash and compile 'disables caching completely' as a safety measure), the cleanup-vs-retrieval race (the 'Missing cache file' counter fires when one instance fetches a file 'while another instance removed the file as part of cache cleanup'), and hardlink corruption (objects stored read-only since 4.0); group-shared caches need umask 002 + setgid + hard_link false. (4) git worktree: one-branch-per-lane is enforced by git itself - 'add refuses to create a new worktree when <commit-ish> is a branch name and is already checked out by another worktree'; per-worktree state is HEAD and index while 'all refs starting with refs/ are shared' plus the object database; detached-HEAD worktrees (-d) sidestep branch ownership entirely (the weco fork's slots use exactly this); git worktree prune clears stale admin entries, git worktree lock protects them, and the add --lock flag exists specifically because locking after add has 'a race condition'; documented limits: submodule 'support is incomplete... NOT recommended to make multiple checkouts of a superproject'. (5) Multi-agent GPU schedulers: three standard fencing modes - MIG (hardware partitioning, up to 7 fully isolated instances per GPU, SMs/L2/memory isolated, requires Ampere+), MPS (concurrent kernel execution, softer isolation, reported up to ~30 percent throughput gain and ~20 percent energy reduction in favorable scenarios, arXiv 2604.22430), and time-slicing (simple round-robin, no isolation); 2025-2026 consensus (kubenatives, Red Hat AI gpu-partitioning-guide, vCluster) is MIG at the tenant boundary and MPS/time-slicing only within a trusted tenant, exposed to Kubernetes as schedulable resources via the device plugin / DRA; spatial co-execution evaluation (arXiv 2511.09143) finds MIG 'generally better suited for multi-tenant settings' precisely because of interference isolation. (6) Cross-lane champion promotion has its own literature: island-model evolutionary computation runs independent subpopulations with periodic migration, and its classic result (Skolicki & de Jong, GECCO 2004) is that too frequent or too large migration collapses global diversity - dominant-island material homogenizes the population; mitigations are sparse/ring topologies (Lissovoi & Witt), coarser migration intervals, and migrating diverse (not only elite) individuals; PBT operationalizes promotion as exploit+explore at worker synchronization points. (7) Parallel coding agents (2025-2026 practice): git worktree per agent is the settled isolation pattern ('one task, one workspace' after mass-merge-conflict incidents with multiple agents in one repo), with the named residual races being shared database state (needs per-worktree DB instances, Upsun guide) and line-based git merge producing false conflicts when two agents add different functions to the same file (OpenAI Codex discussion #13557 proposes entity-level merging; Foremerge, 2026, builds a git-like SQLite coordination protocol with deterministic conflict rules).
lacuna.applicability: Transfers directly to the weco-local long-range runner: (a) Wire the existing consumer_lock into the local loop - the fork already owns the exact primitive (non-blocking flock on .weco/consumer.lock with the refusal message already written); local_optimize/local_cmd simply never calls it, so the fix is fork-level and near-trivial, and it converts today's silent same-workdir double-start (interleaved steps.jsonl, last-writer-wins report.json, two harnesses editing one tree) into a fail-fast refusal. (b) Lane = workdir + GPU lease acquired as one spawn-time act: compose the fork's slots discipline (detached-worktree checkout + uncommitted-state overlay + WECO_SLOT/WECO_PORT_OFFSET env) with gpu-lease's fd-inherited flock, so a lane holds exactly one GPU for exactly as long as its loop process lives - crash-safe with no heartbeat needed; this is the single-host equivalent of Ray's placement group and follows Ray's enforcement lesson: fence via environment (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinned, and empty-string when not granted) because resource REQUESTS are advisory. (c) Shared champion ledger as an Optuna-Journal analog: keep it append-only JSONL with one entry per verdict under a short-lived flock, give every entry a unique id (lane, step, timestamp), make champion promotion itself an entry type that references the winning entry id, and derive report.json by replay rather than treating the overwrite as authoritative; this also matches our existing discipline (vllm_ab_run.py ledger, falsification map) - it only adds locking and entry identity, not new structure. (d) Promotion cadence from PBT/island-model: promote champions only at eval boundaries (never mid-eval), at coarse intervals, and keep falsifications as first-class ledger entries so lanes never re-explore refuted configs - the 2026-09-09 dual-lane record shows this is already the productive pattern (three causal falsifications mapped the config space). (e) The Bazel/CAS lesson for shared artifacts: content-address immutable artifacts (fixtures, checkpoints) by input hash so concurrent producers collide harmlessly with no lock at all. What does NOT transfer: Ray's distributed placement groups and autoscaling (two GPUs on one host need only flock + env pining - a Ray cluster is orders of magnitude too heavy for two lanes); Optuna's RDB/MySQL/GrpcStorageProxy tiers (a DB server buys nothing on a single host; file-lock journal suffices - and the FAQ's SQLite warning is the exact anti-pattern to avoid if the ledger ever grows a DB); MIG (requires Ampere+; this host's cards are TU102/Turing per the plan records, so MIG is unavailable) and MPS (exists on Turing but its soft isolation is the wrong trade for eval determinism - contended evals poison metrics, the eval-sandbox lacuna's subject; only exclusive per-GPU fencing is sound here); time-slicing (no isolation, same objection); semantic/entity-level merge research (interesting, but the cheaper discipline is partitioning file ownership across lanes or using whole-tree slots and resolving at gate time rather than merging). The GPU-collision incident in the 2026-09-10 window is the concrete demonstration that at least the lease wiring is not optional.

design.mechanism: A lane contract assembled from the studied pieces, implementable cold at tools/campaign-runner plus a small fork patch. (1) Lane start: the runner acquires, in fixed order, (i) the consumer lock - call weco/consumer_lock.try_acquire(workdir) (non-blocking flock on <workdir>/.weco/consumer.lock; on None, print the fork's existing refusal line and exit non-zero) - and (ii) the GPU lease - exec through gpu-lease --mode gpu0|gpu1|exclusive, whose flock fds are inherited by the loop process, so the lease is released by process death with no cleanup step; gpu-lease already exports CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and applies --cpuset/--mem-gb. Each lane gets its own .weco workdir (the dual-GPU campaign pattern: one workdir per lane, one GPU per lane), and per-lane env follows the slots.py overlay pattern (a WECO_SLOT-equivalent id and WECO_PORT_OFFSET for any port-touching evals). (2) Ledger: one shared append-only JSONL (the ab-champion-ledger generalized); every append is one json line written while holding flock LOCK_EX on a sibling ledger.lock fd (open, lock, write, flush, unlock - the Optuna Journal pattern); entry = {id: lane+step+timestamp, lane, step, kind: result|falsification|promotion, candidate_tree_sha, metric, gate, verdict, ref: null|prior_entry_id}; promotion entries reference the result entry they crown; reports are projections regenerated by replaying the log, never authoritative state. (3) Promotion rule: a lane may adopt the champion only between steps (never while an eval is in flight - the consumer/slot boundary already marks these points); adoption requires the champion gate (the A/B margin gate vllm_ab_run.py already encodes), and falsification entries are consulted before spawning work so refuted configs are not re-explored. (4) Within a lane, K>1 candidate evals go through the fork's existing slot provider (detached-worktree checkout + overlay), so the lane's own tree is only mutated by the explicit apply step - already the fork's invariant. (5) Hygiene: 'weco slots clean' equivalents plus git worktree prune on a cadence, gpu-lease status in the preflight, and the watchdog treats lease-liveness as the lane's heartbeat (a live flock fd on gpuN.lease proves a live holder; absence after grant means the lane died).
design.failure_modes: (1) Two loops in one .weco workdir (today's fork): the consumer_lock docstring names it - 'Two consumers doing that concurrently in the same tree clobber each other's files mid-eval' - and the corruption is silent: metrics get measured against a tree the other loop is mutating (poisoned verdicts, the eval-sandbox class), steps.jsonl lines interleave so attribution is unrecoverable, and report.json is last-writer-wins. Defense: the lock, fail-fast. (2) GPU collision (already occurred here, 2026-09-10 window): contention noise makes both lanes' numbers non-comparable; defense is the fd-inherited lease plus env pinning, with Ray's caveat honored - pin at spawn time via environment because advisory requests do not bind the eval command. (3) Ledger append interleaving: short single-line writes under O_APPEND are effectively atomic on local filesystems in practice, but POSIX does not guarantee atomicity for regular files at arbitrary lengths, and the whole-file report.json overwrite is never safe under concurrency; NFS additionally breaks flock (Optuna's documented caveat: 'the file locks may not work correctly, which could lead to race conditions'). Defense: locked one-line appends, local disk only, replay-derived reports. (4) Premature convergence via over-promotion: the island-model result (GECCO 2004) - frequent/large migration of champions homogenizes lanes and destroys the diversity that made parallel lanes worth running; defense is coarse promotion intervals, promotion only through the gate, and keeping per-lane exploration alive. (5) Same-file edits across lanes: line-based merge flags even logically independent edits (the false-conflict problem, Codex discussion #13557); defense is ownership partitioning (disjoint files per lane) or whole-tree slots with promotion by re-eval instead of merge. (6) Stale slots/worktrees and disk exhaustion: fork has find_stale_slot_dirs/clean for exactly this; add worktree prune. (7) Cleanup-vs-reader on shared artifacts (ccache's 'Missing cache file' race): prune only entries not content-addressed-current; immutable hash-named artifacts make this benign. (8) Lock-ordering deadlock if more than one lock is ever held: fixed acquisition order (consumer lock, then lease, then ledger lock) - the same discipline gpu-lease already uses (master before per-GPU).
design.effort_estimate: Three small pieces, two of them mostly already written: fork-level - wire consumer_lock.try_acquire into the local loop entry (~10 lines, the primitive and its message already exist in weco/consumer_lock.py); wrapper-level in tools/campaign-runner - the lane starter composing gpu-lease + workdir + env pinning (~100 lines of shell/Python, gpu-lease already exists at the host root); wrapper-level - the locked append-only ledger with entry ids and replay-derived reports (a small extension of the existing vllm_ab_run.py ledger discipline). Doctrine-only: promotion cadence and falsification-consultation rules, which the runbook already practices and only needs written down. Explicitly out of scope: any Ray/Optuna-server/MIG machinery.
design.priority_signal: For: the local loop currently has zero coordination, this host already runs dual-lane windows routinely (three consecutive windows in the MEMORY record), the GPU collision already happened once, and the same-workdir double-start is one mistyped command away from silently poisoning every verdict in a multi-day campaign - the single most expensive failure class this research covers, and every needed primitive (consumer_lock, slots, gpu-lease) already exists in-tree, so the cost is small and bounded. Against: it is a single host with two lanes and an operator present at window open/close, so human arbitration partially covers the gap; heavier coordination machinery (central schedulers, DBs, placement groups) would be overkill and should be refused. Net: high priority for the lock + lease + locked-ledger wiring; deliberately nothing more.
